title: Calvarial Model of Bone Augmentation in Rabbit for Assessment of Bone Growth and Neovascularization in Bone Substitution Materials
protocol: Machine cylinders with lateral stabilizing tabs out of PEEK, having an inner diameter of 5 mm, outer diameter of 8 mm, and height of 5 mm.
Machine PEEK caps designed to clip precisely onto the top of the cylinder (thickness 1 mm).
Sterilize PEEK cylinders and caps by autoclaving before surgery.
Use self-drilling micro screws made of commercial pure titanium (grade 5) with a diameter of 1.2 mm and length of 4 mm for fixing the cylinders.
Sterilize the screws by autoclaving before surgery.
Purchase three-month-old New Zealand white rabbits, weighing approximately 2.5 kg each, for breeding at the University of Geneva.
Acclimate the animals one week prior to surgery.
Provide a prophylactic antibiotic daily (5–10 mg/kg orally) starting 2 h before surgery up to 3 days after surgery.
Sedate the animals by intramuscular injection of ketamine (25 mg/kg, 50 mg/mL, 0.5 mL/kg) + xylazin (3 mg/kg, 20 mg/mL, 0.15 mL/kg).
Wait approximately 20 minutes for the animals to sleep deeply.
Insert an intravenous cannula into the marginal vein from the ear and keep it closed until intubation is completed.
Supply 5% sevoflurane in pure oxygen to maintain anesthesia if the animal shows signs of awakening.
Anesthetize the trachea locally by spraying 10% lidocaine.
Place the rabbit in a prone position and maintain its head in vertical extension.
Slide a small diameter endotracheal tube (2.5 mm) into the rabbit's trachea until airflow can be heard in the tube.
Insert a guide catheter through the small diameter tube to fix the position of the tube in the trachea.
Remove the small diameter tube and slide the definitive endotracheal tube (4.9 mm) over the guide catheter.
Remove the guide and inflate the balloon at the end of the endotracheal tube.
Secure the inflated tube by using a lace tied around the forehead.
Ventilate the animal with 7 mL/kg, frequency of 40/min using 3% sevoflurane in pure oxygen.
Perfuse fentanyl (0.01 mg/mL) through an ear vein at 2–4 mL/h to induce analgesia.
Perfuse propofol (2%) through an ear vein at 4–8 mL/h to induce anesthesia.
Maintain iso-volumetric conditions by perfusing Ringer's acetate at 4 mL/kg/h.
Place a rectal temperature probe for monitoring body temperature.
Monitor heart function, temperature, and oxygen saturation throughout the process.
Control the depth of anesthesia by monitoring autonomous breathing.
Dispense a small bolus of propofol and fentanyl if signs of autonomous breathing are observed.
Place the rabbit on a heated pad (39 °C) covered by a mattress pad on the surgery table.
Shave the scalp.
Apply a lubricating gel on the eyes to avoid irritation and dryness.
Disinfect the site by scrubbing the skin with povidone iodine (10%).
Drape the rabbit with a sterile surgical drape and cut out an access area for the skull.
Disinfect the surgical site with povidone iodine (10%) again.
Apply a lubricating gel on the eyes to avoid irritation and dryness.
Prepare a draped table (sterile drape) for placing the complete surgical tray.
Anesthetize locally with a subcutaneous injection of lidocaine 2%.
Incise through the skin along the calvarial sagittal line from the orbits to the external occipital protuberance.
Ensure that the periosteum is incised.
Gently elevate the periosteum on both sides of the incision.
Rinse the site with sterile saline.
Locate the median and coronal sutures on the skull.
Place the first cylinder on the left upper quadrant, laying it flat.
Fix the cylinder in position with strong hand pressure and screw a micro-screw until resistance is felt.
Ensure that the screw head is flush with the surface of the cylinder tab.
Repeat the procedure to fix the cylinder tightly onto the skull.
Ensure that the cylinder is hermetically fixed to the bone.
Repeat the placement and fixation procedure on the right upper quarter, left lower quarter, and right lower quarter.
Drill 5 intramedullary holes within the area circumscribed by each cylinder.
Drill an intramedullary hole under saline irrigation (0.8 mm in diameter, ~1 mm in depth) with a round bur on the bone, in the center of the area circumscribed by the cylinder.
Ensure that bleeding appears.
Drill two more intramedullary holes along the axis passing through the two tab screws, at the inner edges of the cylinder.
Ensure that bleeding appears.
Along the perpendicular axe, drill two more intramedullary holes at the inner edges of the cylinder.
Ensure that bleeding appears.
Repeat the operation within the three other cylinders.
Prepare the desired bone substitute material according to manufacturer instructions or material specifications.
Fill the first cylinder to the brim with the material sample and close the cylinder by fitting the cap.
Repeat the process in the 3 other cylinders.
Close the skin above the cylinders with an intermittent non-resorbable suture.
Apply a sprayable dressing onto the wound.
Stop analgesia and anesthesia (propofol and fentanyl perfusion arrest) supply and check the recovery of autonomous breathing.
Stop the ventilation once the animal has recovered autonomous breathing.
Maintain the animal under pure oxygen before complete awakening.
Inject buprenorphine hydrochloride SC (0.02 mg/kg, 0.03 mg/mL, 0.67 mL/kg).
Repeat the injection every 6 h for 3 days as post-surgical analgesia.
Transfer the animal into its usual housing with water and complete feeding.
Remove the sutures after about 10 days of wound healing.
